items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The 4th of October, I recorded for a singer named Eddy Howard and the group included ... the famous Charlie Christian on guitar

ctx.x: In August, Benny accepted a job in a dance hall at Coney Island, an amusement park in Long Island, New York, a suburb of New York City, and we played a month there.

A very good friend of the orchestra was a rich young man named John Hammond who came quite often to the Savoy and was the sponsor of Count Basie and was responsible for Basie coming to New York. I had known John for quite sometime and he had also put Charlie Christian in Benny Goodman's orchestra.

One day I received a message from John saying that Teddy Wilson no longer had a big band but was forming a small group to go into a place called Cafe Society down in Greenwich village, a section in lower down town on the west side of New York, and John wanted me to join Teddy because he liked my solo work and probably thought that I'd be happier in a small group where I had more liberty than in a big band, which was true.
